name.description: The rule id: findings join back to it; config rules later in the array override same-named earlier ones.

instructions.description: The yes/no question the model answers, specific to the rule's claim. Required - a generic fallback question would silently recalibrate every reading.

criteria.description: The two-sided contract: true names the exact observable condition for yes, false for no. The defect side decides the handle direction.

anyOf.description: A qualified capture address {grammar}:{capture} (e.g. markdown:section): targets the named grammar's own capture. Unknown grammar or capture is a setup error.
A qualified capture address {grammar}:{capture} (e.g. markdown:section): targets the named grammar's own capture. Unknown grammar or capture is a setup error.

Score handler (score rules only): one level per criteria entry, indexed by score 0..N. Direction is expressed by the map itself (high-bad: [pass, pass, warn, error]; high-good: [error, warn, pass, pass]). The length MUST equal the criteria count and at least one level must be non-pass. An optional per-tier message (author feedback) becomes the finding's note when the tier fires; absent = a bare finding.

message.description: The rule author's feedback; the finding's note when this tier fires.

anyOf.description: Choice handler (choice rules only): one tier per option label, keyed by the label. The option probabilities are summed per tier; the tier with the most probability is the verdict, and its most probable option's message becomes the finding's note. Options are unordered, nothing is averaged. The labels MUST equal the criteria labels and at least one tier must be non-pass. Optional undecided { margin, level, message? }: when the top tier's probability leads the runner-up tier's by less than `margin` (between 0 and 1), this tier fires instead - an undecided reading the rule acts on like any other tier.

message.description: The rule author's feedback; the finding's note when this tier fires.

anyOf.description: Noul handler (noul rules only): per-threshold comparison operators declare the direction. Declare at least one tier - warn, error, or both; a handle with neither is rejected. An error-only handle fires error past its threshold and passes otherwise. When both tiers are present, warn is the wider region and error the strictly narrower one (same direction, ordered toward the defect: greater warn < greater error, or less warn > less error). silent_band [lo, hi] keeps raw-p readings inside it silent (must be ordered, must not cover the whole scale, must not contain any declared threshold value); absent = everything surfaces.

warn.description: One threshold comparison: exactly one operator. The operator IS the defect direction - greater_than fires on high readings, less_than on low ones. Within (0, 1).

anyOf.description: Fires when the raw value is strictly greater.

apiKey.description: The API key. Precedence: this, else $JINT_PROVIDER_KEY. Never written to a run record.

url.description: The Decisions endpoint the questions are posted to; it must end in /decisions. Precedence: this, else $JINT_PROVIDER_URL, else https://api.openai.com/v1/decisions.

concurrency.description: Max in-flight classifier calls, run-wide (the wall-clock knob). Default 16 (measured: 53.9 rps at 16, zero 429s), max 64.

timeout.description: Per-call classifier timeout, seconds (liveness, not retry - the SDK owns retries). Default 30 (~80x the measured p95 of 380ms). A hung call becomes a per-element PROVIDER_TIMEOUT failure.
